newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary modifies draft budget, deficit unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Hungary modifies draft budget, deficit unchanged.

text.p: Hungary's government modified certain income targets of the draft 1997 budget on Thursday but the changes will not increase the budget deficit, government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference.
"The measures altogether result in a breaking even compared with the original plans," Kiss, Secretary of State in the Prime Minister's office, said on Thursday.
He added that the government decided on the modifications after hearing proposals during the discussion of the draft budget in Parliament.
Of the amendments those which affect the social security will lead to the largest change.
"But put together, the changes will result in a breakeven social security budget, as originally planned," Kiss said.

The government decided to reduce the rate of social security contributions paid by employers to 39 percent in the draft budget instead of the previously planned 41 percent. The current rate is 42.5 percent.

Within the 41 percent rate a 13 percent chunk should have included a 4,500-forint monthly minimum payment. But the government is abolishing that in favour of an 1,800 forint minimum monthly payment, over the 39 percent of actual wages.
The 4,500 forint minimum had been sharply criticised because it was widely believed to increase the burden of enterprises which pay low wages to employees.
